Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At distance $r$ from O: a full circle gives $\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2r}$, a semicircle $\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4r}$, an infinite straight wire $\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}$, a semi-infinite wire with O on the perpendicular through its end $\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}$, and a wire whose line passes through O gives zero.

A: the straight wire passes O at distance $r$ and gives $\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}$ out of the page; the full circle is traversed clockwise and gives $\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2r}$ into the page.

$B_{0}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2r}-\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{2πr}(π-1)\Rightarrow \text{A-III}$

B: the two semi-infinite wires end at the ends of the semicircle, and all three parts give fields out of the page.

$B_{0}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}+\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4r}+\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}(π+2)\Rightarrow \text{B-I}$

C: the horizontal semi-infinite wire and the semicircle both give fields into the page; the vertical wire lies on a line through O and gives zero.

$B_{0}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}+\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4r}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4πr}(π+1)\Rightarrow \text{C-IV}$

D: both straight wires lie on a line through O and give zero, leaving only the semicircle.

$B_{0}=\dfrac{μ_{0}I}{4r}\Rightarrow \text{D-II}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: In Young's double slits experiment, the position of 5${}^{\mathrm{th}}$ bright fringe from the central maximum is 5 cm. The distance between slits and screen is 1 m and wavelength of used monochromatic light is 600 nm. The separation between the slits is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between the slits and the screen, $L=1\text{m}$, the wavelength of the light, $λ=600\text{nm}=600\times 10^{-9}\text{m}$, and the position of the 5th bright fringe from the central maximum, $y=5\text{cm}=0.05\text{m}$.

The distance between the central maximum and the $n$th bright fringe is given by the formula:

$y_{n}=\frac{nλL}{d}$

where $d$ is the distance between the two slits.

We can rearrange this formula to solve for $d$:

$d=\frac{nλL}{y_{n}}$

Substituting the values given in the question, we get:

$d=\frac{5\times 600\times 10^{-9}\times 1\times 100}{5}$

$d=6\times 10^{-5}\text{m}$

$d=60μ\text{m}$

Therefore, the separation between the slits is $60μ\text{m}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text: T is the time period of simple pendulum on the earth's surface. Its time period becomes $x$ T when taken to a height R (equal to earth's radius) above the earth's surface. Then, the value of $x$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At surface of earth time period

$\mathrm{T}=2π\sqrt{\frac{\ell }{\mathrm{g}}}$

At height $\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{R}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{g}^{'}=\dfrac{\mathrm{g}}{\left (1+\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{R}}\right )^{2}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{g}}{4} \\  \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{xT}=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{\ell }{(\mathrm{g}/4)}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{xT}=2\times 2π\sqrt{\dfrac{\ell }{\mathrm{g}}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{xT}=2\mathrm{T}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text:
Assume that the earth is a solid sphere of uniform density and a tunnel is dug along its diameter throughout the earth. It is found that when a particle is released in this tunnel, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The mass of the particle is 100 g. The time period of the motion of the particle will be (approximately)

(Take g = 10 m s${}^{-2}$ , radius of earth = 6400 km)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Gravitational acceleration at a distance of $r$ from centre of earth is given by

$g^{'}=\frac{g}{R}r$

Where $R$ is the radius of earth

So, $\frac{d^{2}r}{dt^{2}}=-\frac{g}{R}r$

$\Rightarrow \quad T=2π\sqrt{\frac{R}{g}}=2π\sqrt{\frac{6400000}{10}}$

$=2π\times 800\sec$

$=5024\sec$

= 1 hour 24 minutes (approx.)

text:
An object of mass 8 kg is hanging from one end of a uniform rod CD of mass 2 kg and length 1 m pivoted at its end C on a vertical wall as shown in figure. It is supported by a cable AB such that the system is in equilibrium. The tension in the cable is (Take g = 10 m/s${}^{2}$)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rod's weight $2\times 10=20\text{N}$ acts at its midpoint, 0.5 m from the pivot C; the block's weight $8\times 10=80\text{N}$ acts at end D, $60+40=100\text{cm}=1.0\text{m}$ from C.

The cable meets the rod at B, 0.6 m from the wall, at $30^{\circ }$. Its horizontal component acts along the rod through the pivot and has no moment; its vertical component $T\sin 30^{\circ }=\dfrac{T}{2}$ has a moment arm of 0.6 m.

Torque balance about C:

$\dfrac{T}{2}\times 0.6=20\times 0.5+80\times 1.0=90\text{N m}$

$T=\dfrac{90}{0.3}=300\text{N}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: In an LC oscillator, if values of inductance and capacitance become twice and eight times, respectively, then the resonant frequency of oscillator becomes $x$ times its initial resonant frequency $ω_{0}$. The value of $x$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

So $\mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{4}$

text: If $\vec{P}=3\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{Q}=4\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2.5\widehat{k}$ then, the unit vector in the direction of $\vec{P}\times \vec{Q}$ is $\frac{1}{x}\left (\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\sqrt{3}\widehat{k}\right )$. The value of $x$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$⃗{P}=3\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$

$⃗{Q}=4\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2.5\hat{k}$

$⃗{P}\times ⃗{Q}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 4 & \sqrt{3} & 2.5 \end{array}\right |$

$=\hat{i}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )-\hat{j}\left (-\frac{1}{2}\right )+\hat{k}(-\sqrt{3})$

$=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{\hat{j}}{2}-\sqrt{3}\hat{k}$

$|⃗{P}\times ⃗{Q}|=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+3}=2$

Unit vector along $⃗{P}\times ⃗{Q}=\frac{1}{4}(\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\sqrt{3}\hat{k})$

$x=4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

text: The wavelength of the radiation emitted is $λ_{0}$ when an electron jumps from the second excited state to the first excited state of hydrogen atom. If the electron jumps from the third excited state to the second orbit of the hydrogen atom, the wavelength of the radiation emitted will be $\frac{20}{x}λ_{0}$. The value of $x$ is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Second excited state $\to$ first excited state , $n=3$ to $n=2$

$\frac{1}{λ_{0}}=R\left (\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right )=\left (\frac{5R}{36}\right )$

Third excited state $\to$ second orbit , $n=4$ to $n=2$

$\frac{1}{λ}=R\left (\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right )=\left (\frac{3}{16}R\right )$

Taking ratio of (1) and (2)

$\frac{λ}{λ_{0}}=\frac{5}{36}\times \frac{16}{3}=\left (\frac{20}{27}\right )$

$λ=\frac{20}{27}λ_{0}$

$x=27$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, Length, $L=62.8\mathrm{cm}$ 

diameter, $d=4\mathrm{mm}$ 

radius, $r=2\mathrm{mm}$ 

$y=x\times 10^{4}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$


[IMG]


According to graph, $\Delta l/f=\tan 45^{\circ }=1$ 

$Y=\frac{FL}{A\cdot \Delta L}$ 

$Y=\frac{1\times 62.8\times 10^{-2}}{3.14\times 2\times 2\times 10^{-6}}=5\times 10^{4}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$

$\therefore$ x = 5

text:
An LCR series circuit of capacitance 62.5 nF and resistance of 50 $\Omega$, is connected to an A.C. source of frequency 2.0 kHz. For maximum value of amplitude of current in circuit, the value of inductance is $__________ mH$.

(Take $π^{2}=10$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ For maximum amplitude of current, circuit should be at resonance.

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore X_{L}=X_{C} \\  \\ ωL=\dfrac{1}{ωC} \\  \\ L=\dfrac{1}{ω^{2}C} \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{\left (2π\times 2\times 10^{3}\right )^{2}\times 62.5\times 10^{-9}} \\  \\ =100\mathrm{mH} \end{array}$

In the given circuit, the equivalent resistance between the terminal A and B is $__________$ $\Omega$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Both $4\Omega$ resistance and left $2\Omega$ resistance get short-circuited. So, no current will flow through them.

Remove the resistors that have no current. Now the equivalent circuit becomes -


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=3+(2\|2)+6 \\  \\ \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=3+1+6 \\  \\ \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=10\Omega  \end{array}$

text:
A uniform electric field of 10 N/C is created between two parallel charged plates (as shown in figure). An electron enters the field symmetrically between the plates with a kinetic energy 0.5 eV. The length of each plate is 10 cm. The angle ($θ$) of deviation of the path of electron as it comes out of the field is $___________ ($in degree).


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} 0.5\mathrm{e}=\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{x}}^{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}} \\  \\ \text{Along}\mathrm{x}\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}}\mathrm{t} \\  \\ \text{Along y}\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{eE}}{\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{t} \\  \\ \mathrm{dividing}\dfrac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}}{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{E}\sqrt{\dfrac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}}=\mathrm{E}v_{\mathrm{x}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \tan θ=\dfrac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}}=\mathrm{E}\times \mathrm{L}=10\times 0.1=1 \\  \\ θ=45^{\circ } \end{array}$
